method: Qur'anic verse themes compared with identified earlier scriptural passages using online English translations; no original-language text/edition comparison or manuscript-dating review completed.

rows.note: A general Semitic religious invocation is not enough to establish a direct earlier verse-specific parallel; further primary-liturgical source checks needed.

rows.theme: Praise of the Lord of worlds

candidates.shared: Both praise God's greatness and exalted status.
candidates.difference: Psalm is a first-person acrostic praise hymn of the kingly God; Qur'an 1:2 addresses God as Lord of the worlds.
candidates.caution: Common prayer vocabulary; not proof of literary dependence.

candidates.shared: Both describe God in terms of mercy and compassion.
candidates.difference: Psalm adds patience or slowness to anger and covenantal lovingkindness; Qur'an 1:3 repeats the dual mercy epithets.
candidates.caution: Broad formula also occurs elsewhere in Hebrew scripture; primary-language and textual formula review outstanding.

rows.theme: God's authority on the Day of Judgment

candidates.shared: Judgment and the distinction between righteous and wicked appear in both.
candidates.difference: Psalm 1 depicts the fate of righteous and wicked people, whereas Qur'an 1:4 identifies God as sovereign on judgment day.
candidates.caution: Conceptual not an episode-specific textual parallel; consider whether to surface as context only.

candidates.shared: Exclusive devotion to God and the desire for God's help and guidance form a devotional context.
candidates.difference: Psalm 86 prays within a longer appeal for rescue; Qur'an 1:5 uniquely combines direct exclusive worship and assistance in a balanced formulation.
candidates.caution: Not a close quotation. Compare other Jewish/Christian prayer traditions before promoting.

rows.theme: Petition for guidance on the right path

candidates.shared: Both petitions ask God for guidance along the right ways or paths.
candidates.difference: Psalm 25 asks to learn God's ways and truth in first person singular; Qur'an 1:6 requests guidance on the singular straight path in plural voice.
candidates.caution: A comparatively close prayer motif, still not evidence of direct dependence.

rows.theme: Path of the favored versus the erring

candidates.shared: Both distinguish the righteous path from the way of those who stray or incur negative judgment.
candidates.difference: Psalm 1 contrasts two kinds of conduct and their consequences; Qur'an 1:7 petitions guidance along the way of those God favors, avoiding anger and misguidance.
candidates.caution: Do not equate the identities of the groups or imply the same referents.
